name: Alprostadil

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Raises cAMP in penile smooth muscle (label)

what.text: Alprostadil is the drug form of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), a natural fatty-acid messenger. For erectile dysfunction (ED) it is injected into the side of the penis (intracavernosal injection), as Caverject and Edex, or was placed in the urethra as a small pellet, as Muse. A different alprostadil product, Prostin VR Pediatric, is an infusion for newborns with certain heart defects.
How it acts, according to the FDA label

items.text: Alprostadil binds its receptors in the penis and raises a messenger called cAMP. This relaxes the spongy smooth muscle and widens the penile arteries.
The spaces in the penis fill with blood, which presses the small veins shut and traps the blood (the veno-occlusive mechanism).

what.text: Alprostadil is also one of the three drugs in compounded "Trimix" injections, together with papaverine and phentolamine. Trimix is not an FDA-approved product (see US position).

research.text: Injected and urethral alprostadil were tested in placebo-controlled trials in the 1990s. Two large published reports, the label's own trials and one study comparing it with a compounded three-drug mix are listed below as they were run.

research.meta: USA · 1996 · Three studies: placebo-controlled dose-response, then open-label self-injection
research.title: Injected alprostadil (NEJM 1996)

facts.v: Linet OI, Ogrinc FG; Alprostadil Study Group. N Engl J Med 1996;334(14):873-7
three multi-center, prospective studies, including a placebo-controlled dose-response study and a 6-month self-injection study
296 men in the dose-response study; 683 men in the self-injection study. ED of vascular, nerve, psychological and mixed causes.
injections of alprostadil into the penis, at a range of doses, or placebo
up to 6 months
clinic and lab ratings of erection; whether sexual activity was possible and satisfactory, rated by men and partners

research.found: All doses did better than placebo, with a dose-response (P ≤ 0.001). In the 6-month study, men reported sexual activity was possible after 94% of injections. Penile pain occurred at some time in 50% of men, prolonged erection in 5%, priapism in 1%, penile scarring (fibrosis) in 2%, and bruising or blood collection in 8%.

research.title: Urethral alprostadil, Muse (NEJM 1997)

facts.v: Padma-Nathan H, Hellstrom WJ, Kaiser FE, et al.; MUSE Study Group. N Engl J Med 1997;336(1):1-7
in-clinic dose testing, then men who responded were randomized to their dose or placebo at home
1,511 men aged 27 to 88 with long-standing ED from physical causes; 996 responded in the clinic and 961 reported home results
alprostadil 125 to 1,000 micrograms placed in the urethra, or placebo
3 months at home
whether men had intercourse successfully at least once

research.found: 64.9% of men on alprostadil (299 of 461) had intercourse at least once, vs 18.6% on placebo (93 of 500, P < 0.001). Mild penile pain followed 10.8% of doses. Low blood pressure occurred in the clinic in 3.3% of men. No priapism or penile fibrosis was seen.

research.title: Caverject trials described in the FDA label

facts.v: Study 1: 2.5-week randomized, double-blind crossover vs placebo, then dose finding and 4 weeks at home. Study 2: double-blind, parallel groups, single dose. Study 3: 6-month open-label.
153 men aged 23 to 69 (Study 1); 296 men aged 21 to 74 (Study 2)
Caverject 2.5 to 20 micrograms or placebo, injected into the penis
full rigidity on exam, and a rigidity monitor (RigiScan)

research.found: No man responded to placebo. Response rose with dose. In Study 1, 76% responded by clinical exam and 51% by RigiScan; 73% of home injections in 102 men led to satisfactory intercourse.

research.title: Compounded Trimix vs alprostadil alone (Int J Impot Res 2005)

facts.v: Seyam R, Mohamed K, Akhras AA, Rashwan H. Int J Impot Res 2005;17(4):346-53
prospective; 9 groups of Trimix doses; each man got alprostadil 20 micrograms and one Trimix dose, 1 week apart
180 men with ED; mean age 50.5; 91% with a physical cause
Trimix (phentolamine 1 mg, alprostadil 2.5 to 10 micrograms, papaverine 5 to 20 mg) vs alprostadil alone
two clinic visits
penile artery flow on ultrasound, rigidity, satisfaction, time to go down, side effects

research.found: Blood flow, rigidity, pain and satisfaction did not differ significantly. Trimix gave longer erections and more priapism than alprostadil alone.

research.text: Trimix and Bimix are compounded mixtures, not FDA-approved products.

us.text: Alprostadil is FDA approved, by prescription, for erectile dysfunction as Caverject (1995), Edex (1997) and Caverject Impulse (2002), all injected into the penis. Muse (1996), the urethral form, is listed as discontinued. Compounded Trimix is not FDA approved. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: approved July 6, 1995 (NDA 020379), with priority review. Approved uses: treatment of ED, and as an add-on to other tests in diagnosing ED.
approved June 12, 1997 (NDA 020649). Approved use: ED of nerve, blood-vessel, psychological or mixed cause.
a dual-chamber syringe form, approved June 11, 2002 (NDA 021212), for ED and as a diagnostic add-on.
the urethral pellet, approved November 19, 1996 (NDA 020700). FDA's data now list every Muse strength as discontinued, and the search found no current Muse label on DailyMed.
approved October 16, 1981 (NDA 018484) to keep a newborn's ductus arteriosus open until heart surgery. It is not an ED product.

the Caverject label says the safety and efficacy of combining it with other vasoactive drugs injected into the penis have not been established, and the risks of prolonged erection, priapism and low blood pressure may be higher. The Edex label advises against such combinations.

a compounded injection of alprostadil, papaverine and phentolamine. No FDA-approved Trimix product exists, and papaverine itself has no FDA approval (see the papaverine page). FDA lists alprostadil and phentolamine mesylate as components of approved drugs, and papaverine hydrochloride as not, among bulk substances under evaluation for outsourcing-facility (503B) compounding.

FDA says compounded drugs are not FDA approved, which means FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed.

world.lead: Alprostadil for ED is an approved prescription medicine in the US, Canada, Australia and EU countries such as Ireland. There is no EU-wide (EMA) authorisation; products are authorised country by country. The UK status was not confirmed. It is not on WADA's Prohibited List.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Caverject 1995, Edex 1997, Caverject Impulse 2002, all ED; Muse 1996, now discontinued). Prescription-only.

Approved medicine. Caverject (injection into the penis) and Prostin VR are listed as marketed, prescription. Vitaros cream is listed as approved (2015). Muse was cancelled after marketing in May 2026.

after.text: Alprostadil is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is not in the 2027 Monitoring Program either. Class S0 covers only substances with no current government approval for human therapeutic use, and alprostadil is approved for some use (see above).

side.text: The label lists penile pain as the most common side effect. Serious risks include prolonged erection and priapism, which can cause permanent damage if not treated, and scarring of the penis (penile fibrosis).

items.text: in Caverject studies of 1,861 men treated up to 18 months, erections of 4 to 6 hours occurred in 4% and priapism (over 6 hours) in 0.4%. The label says untreated priapism can cause penile tissue damage and permanent loss of potency, and that men with sickle cell disease or trait, multiple myeloma or leukemia must not use it.

scarring of the penis was reported in 3% of men overall in Caverject studies, and in 7.8% in one self-injection study of up to 18 months. The Edex label reports 7.8% over up to 24 months, including Peyronie's disease. Both labels say to examine the penis regularly and stop if angulation or fibrosis develops.
penile pain (37% of men on Caverject; 2% on placebo; 3% stopped for pain), bruising or blood collection at the site (2% to 3%), penile rash or swelling (1%).
alprostadil can reach the bloodstream and lower blood pressure, especially in men with venous leak. Three men (0.2%) on Caverject stopped for symptomatic low blood pressure; dizziness occurred in 1%.
men on blood thinners such as warfarin or heparin may bleed more at the injection site.
men with penile deformation, angulation, fibrosis or Peyronie's disease, and (Edex) men with penile implants.
mild penile pain after 10.8% of doses and low blood pressure in the clinic in 3.3% of men.
in one randomized comparison, the compounded three-drug mix caused longer erections and more priapism than alprostadil alone.

FDA's status for alprostadil cream (Vitaros) was not confirmed; openFDA lists no approved alprostadil cream.

The approved uses of Vitaros in Canada and Ireland, and of Neupedix in Australia, were not read from their product information.
surprises: Muse, the urethral alprostadil pellet often listed as an ED option, is shown as discontinued in FDA's data, and Health Canada cancelled its Muse listings in May 2026.
